clue.text: Anti-mosquito sprays, wrong price?

definitions.note: a misquoted price is a wrong quotation; the question mark flags the price sense of quote

indicators.note: sprays suggests the letters of the first word are scattered about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that insect-repellent sprays have been priced incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anti-mosquito' looks like a description of the sprays, but its twelve letters are the fodder; the answer's letters come from rearranging them.
explanation.definitionFit: A quotation is also a price estimate, so a mistaken one is a misquotation, here read whimsically.

clue.text: Frustrating experiences for some horses

parts.note: bad dreams are night- plus a word for female horses, so this word alone is what remains of them

explanation.walkthrough: Bad dreams are nightmares; drop 'night' and the word is the female horses themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Female horses are the second half of the word for terrible dreams, a playful pairing.

clue.text: Where Steps are playing, writes a couple of lines

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are tossed about and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L stands for line, so two lines give LL

explanation.surface: The pop group Steps are performing while someone jots down a couple of lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Steps is a British pop group, but the capital disguises plain stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the vertical shaft in a building that houses a staircase.

clue.text: In Paris, one spring, without any ties?

parts.note: un is French for one
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Someone in Paris springs free, completely unattached.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbound means not tied up or restrained, so free of any ties.

clue.text: Tram cheap, but MP going for the tube

indicators.note: going means leaving, so those two letters are taken out of the phrase

parts.note: taken as written: the letters of MP

explanation.surface: A cheap tram, but the politician prefers the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The tube' looks like London's Underground; it is the windpipe. Take M and P out of TRAMCHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the air tube linking the throat to the lungs.

clue.text: Maybe Turner portrait in art exhibits

indicators.note: exhibits says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Turner painting is on show in a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter JMW Turner, but it is the singer Tina Turner, whose first name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tina Turner was a famous singer, so Tina is an example of someone named Turner.

clue.text: Yawning in front of Met, looking innocent

indicators.note: in front of puts the first piece before the second

parts.note: yawning means gaping or open
faced means met or confronted

explanation.surface: Someone yawns before the Metropolitan Police, trying to look guiltless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' looks like the London police; it is the verb, to have faced.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-faced person has a frank, guileless expression suggesting innocence.

clue.text: Only daughter, say, brought up having kittens?

parts.note: one means only, single

indicators.note: brought up, in a down clue, means the letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: An only daughter, raised alongside a litter of kittens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having kittens' is British slang for being very anxious; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on edge is to be nervous, as the idiom having kittens means being agitated.

clue.text: Evil influence? No doubt about it!

parts.note: ill means evil or harm
to have a say is to have influence

explanation.surface: Someone declares a bad influence is beyond question.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation I'll say is an emphatic agreement meaning certainly.

clue.text: Not entirely routine opera

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is not given in full: its last letter is cut off

parts.note: routine, as an adjective, means normal or ordinary

explanation.surface: A not-quite-standard production of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: NORMAL loses its final L to leave the title of Bellini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a well-known opera by Bellini about a Druid priestess.

clue.text: Artist in boring book group, bit of a thinker

indicators.note: boring is read as drilling into, so the first pieces are driven inside the others

parts.note: a cell is a small group within an organisation
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist sits in on a tedious book club.
explanation.walkthrough: RA and IN together bore into B plus CELL, giving B + RAIN + CELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain cell is a small part of the organ that thinks, so a bit of a thinker.

clue.text: Swallow sheltering is tense and agitated

indicators.note: sheltering means holding something inside, so the swallow word contains the other pieces

parts.note: a draught is a single swallow of drink
taken as written
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A bird taking cover looks nervous and flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird, but it is a gulp of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraught describes someone deeply upset and troubled, the same state as agitated.

clue.text: Mysterious vessels circled around by Valparaiso funicular

indicators.note: circled around says the letters held by the next words are read in the opposite direction
by is read as 'held by', so the answer is held within the following words

parts.note: the letters sit across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Strange craft seem to orbit a cable railway in the Chilean port of Valparaiso.
explanation.walkthrough: SOFU straddles the two words; read backwards it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects are often imagined as alien spacecraft, mysterious vessels of the sky.

clue.text: Intellectual English master inspiring good grades at first

indicators.note: inspiring is read as breathing in, so the outer pieces take the initials inside

parts.note: a head or headmaster is the master of a school

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: initials of good and grades

explanation.surface: An English teacher motivates students to get top marks early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' is the head teacher of a school, not a degree or expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is a colloquial name for a highly academic, bookish person.

clue.text: Some stars are irritating on the radio show

indicators.note: on the radio says the words are heard spoken, so their sound-alike is written

parts.note: they grate means they are irritating
to bear is to show or display, as a document bears a signature

explanation.surface: Some radio stars are annoying on a broadcast programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities, but means real stars; 'show' looks like a radio programme but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear, Ursa Major, is a constellation containing the Plough, a group of stars.

clue.text: A new bridge, the end of lorry chaos?

parts.note: an arch is the curved span of a bridge

indicators.note: the end of picks out the final letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of lorry

explanation.surface: A newly opened bridge might mean the end of traffic chaos caused by lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end of lorry chaos' reads as one phrase, but only the last letter of 'lorry' is used, leaving 'chaos' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a state of lawless disorder, so complete chaos.

clue.text: A single drunk in support group finds relief from pain

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the support group letters

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a support group

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: One intoxicated person at Alcoholics Anonymous finds comfort from suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A single' looks like a quantity of drink, but both words are the fodder for 'drunk'.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for the absence of pain sensation, achieved by painkillers.

clue.text: Old record of Hull account

parts.note: a hull is an outer casing or shell, as of a seed

explanation.surface: An old record from the city of Hull's past ledger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' looks like the Yorkshire city, but it is the husk or shell of a seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Early gramophone records were made of shellac, so the resin names the old 78 discs.

clue.text: It's ref breaking up fighting

indicators.note: breaking up implies the letters are split apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A referee is pulling apart players who are brawling.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife means conflict or angry disagreement, the noun sense of fighting.

clue.text: Charlie and Wayne briefly getting first glimpse of reed warbler

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Wayne Rooney is an English footballer

indicators.note: first glimpse of takes the initial letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter of reed

explanation.surface: Two footballers spot a reed warbler, a small bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reed warbler' reads as the bird, but 'warbler' alone is the definition. Wayne Rooney is a former England footballer; drop his surname's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crooner sings in a soft, sentimental style, so is a warbler, a singer.

clue.text: Ancestor's majestic public address

parts.note: grand means imposing or majestic
PA is the abbreviation for public address system

explanation.surface: A forefather gives an impressive public speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Ancestor' stands for 'is' and links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is a forebear one generation further back than a parent.

clue.text: Occasionally grabs stark inch of stomach

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so every other letter is taken from the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone sometimes grabs an inch of bare belly fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric is the adjective describing things relating to the stomach.

clue.text: Hot actor, extremely hollow

indicators.note: extremely means taking only the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of actor
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: A sexy actor with a gaunt look.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate or burning with feeling, a figurative sense of hot.

clue.text: Stylish establishment warrants reporting

indicators.note: reporting suggests the word is spoken out, so a word that sounds the same is entered

parts.note: writs are legal warrants or orders

explanation.surface: A smart hotel is served with court orders, as the press relays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ritz is a famously luxurious London hotel, a byword for an upmarket venue.

clue.text: One providing security, in the main

definitions.text: One providing security, in the main

parts.words: One providing security, in the main
parts.note: in the main reads as 'mostly' but means at sea, the main being the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' seems to mean 'chiefly', but the main is the sea: this guard keeps watch over shores and waters.
explanation.definitionFit: This service patrols the shoreline and sea to keep vessels and swimmers safe.

clue.text: Pretend to be riding horse around

parts.note: to act is to pretend
up means riding, as a jockey is up on a horse

explanation.surface: Someone pretends to be on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' looks like part of the riding picture, but horse around is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or fool about, which is what horsing around means.

clue.text: Separated from wife, watch out for gossip

indicators.note: out suggests the remaining letters are disordered, put out of place
separated from means the wife letter is taken away from the word

explanation.surface: A divorced man warns someone to beware of rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: Take W from WATCH to leave ATCH, then rearrange it. 'Watch out' looks like a warning but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal talk, much like a gossip as a noun.

clue.text: Restorative instilling energy before noon in first-year student

indicators.note: instilling means putting something into, so the student word takes the others inside

parts.note: a fresher is a British university student in the first year

indicators.note: before places the energy letter ahead of the noon letter

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tonic gives new students energy before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: A fresher is a first-year university student in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshener revives or refreshes, so it is restorative, taken here as a noun.

clue.text: Was model wearing shiny fabric?

parts.note: an artist's model sits for a painter, so 'was model' gives sat
in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'

explanation.surface: A model posed in a glossy outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth cloth with a glossy surface on one side.

clue.text: Spread wrist with cream around radius softly for this?

definitions.text: Spread wrist with cream around radius softly for this?

indicators.note: spread signals the following letters are spread out and reassembled
around adds that the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Advice to rub cream gently on the wrist, round the forearm bone, to ease an ache.
explanation.walkthrough: The radius is also the forearm bone beside the wrist, so the whole clue pictures a remedy for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Writer's cramp is a painful hand and wrist spasm from too much writing, which a soothing cream might treat.
